The hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis provides physiological adaptations to different types of external and internal stresses, ensuring homeostasis within mammals through intricate hormonal regulation. Environmental stimuli such as maternal care during early life stages or dietary changes can significantly influence the functioning capacity of this critical system via epigenetic mechanisms—modifications that do not alter DNA sequence but affect gene expression. These modifications are important because they enable an organism to adapt more quickly in response to future stressors based on earlier experiences. For example, if a mammal undergoes significant early-life challenges or prolonged periods without proper nutrition during developmental critical windows (like prenatal development and postnatal life), its HPA axis may develop heightened sensitivity as part of survival strategies. Epigenetic mechanisms primarily include DNA methylation changes near promoteRs to reduce transcription factor binding; histone modifications like acetylation, which loosens chromatin structure making genes more accessible for activation or deactivation based on environmental input signals. The selective detection method mentioned here is based on hydrophilicity interaction liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (HILIC-LC-MS). This technique allows us to identify and quantify thiram residues specifically, even when the sample matrix contains a variety of other compounds. In surface extraction processes for fruit vegetables that contain complex mixtures like carbohydrates or proteins which can potentially interfere in our analysis process; HPLCs with specific columns (e.g., C18) are often used to separate these components before they enter into LC-MS system. However, thiram has a unique property of hydrophobicity due its chemical structure. It doesn't interact well under conventional reversed phase chromatography conditions but does preferentially bind onto the stationary phases in HILIC-LC systems that are enriched with polar substances such as silica or diethylamine bonding materials. In this process, after surface extraction and preliminary purification steps to remove non-target components; thiram is then separated from other potential interferences by a hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography column. The analytes in the resulting eluent are subsequently ionized using an electrospray source for mass spectrometry detection. This method ensures that only compounds with similar properties (i.e., those interacting strongly and selectively) to thiram, will be detected by MS system thus reducing false positives or negatives.
